facts.F93: Aggregate and owners. A note is a child of the Report aggregate and is reached only through its owner and report id (a note reached through another report or owner finds nothing). Each decision has one owner: text normalisation, length bound, creation and revision sit on ReportNote (Write, Revise); who may change a note sits on the new kernel value NoteSignature, shared by ReportNote and DeliveryNote so the Delivery rule is decided once; refusals and ordering sit in ReportNoteCommands and ReportNoteQueries; write access on the owner stays a route guard (RbacGuard TeamWrite or PortfolioWrite), read access a TeamRead or PortfolioRead guard on the controller.
facts.F95: Concurrency: confirmed, the last save wins, as for Delivery notes. A note carries no concurrency token and a note change never touches the Report concurrency token, so adding or editing a note cannot conflict with an edit of the report. A change or delete of a note that another writer deleted meanwhile is translated in ReportRepository (DbUpdateConcurrencyException becomes a false save) into the port outcome NotFound, so no EF type reaches Application (R-RP5).
facts.F96: Deleting a Team or Portfolio: confirmed from the code. Reports carry cascade foreign keys to Teams and Portfolios (LighthouseAppContext ConfigureReports) and single and bulk report removal both end in IReportWriter.Remove plus one save (ReportCommands.Delete, ReportBulkRemover). ReportNotes gets a cascade foreign key to Reports, so notes follow in all three paths with no code of their own. The author foreign key to UserProfiles is SetNull, as for Delivery notes, so removing a person keeps the note and its captured name.
facts.F98: Time stays out of Application. ReportNoteCommands takes the instant as an argument and the read record carries instants; the controller holds ILighthouseClock, passes now and reduces CreatedAt and LastEditedAt to the instance-zone day in the DTO, as DeliveryNoteDto does.
